reviews.reasoning: Re-derived rather than trusted. The hodu-le-YHWH verse-initial claim at oshb:Ps.136.1 (“הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי…”) collates at byte tier; swept against the full six-member book-wide list (33:2, 105:1, 107:1 spelled defectively, 118:1, 118:29, 136:1) directly from source — all six open with the imperative, confirming the row's count. Swept the closing refrain “לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ” across all 26 verses of the psalm from verse_map_oshb.json: present in 26 of 26, with the defective spelling of the second word (no vav) at exactly one verse, oshb:Ps.136.3 (“לְעֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ”), and plene at every other verse — the row's spelling claim is exact rather than approximate. The imperative-plus-object frame of this span (hodu + escalating divine titles) does give way to a participial construction at web:Ps.136.4, a genuine grammatical-form seam, so the rejected_alternative's refusal to fold 136:4 in is well grounded. Considered whether unit_type "refrain_unit" overclaims, since the refrain is uniform across all 26 verses of the psalm and cannot itself be the differentiator between this row and its neighbors; on reflection this looks like a defensible literary-form label naming the psalm's own governing device (Ps 136 is the Psalter's paradigm litany-refrain composition) rather than a claim that the refrain positions this row's own edges, so it is not pressed as a defect.

The cited participial form at oshb:Ps.136.5 (“לְעֹשֵׂ֣ה הַ֭שָּׁמַיִם בִּתְבוּנָ֑ה…”) collates at byte tier. Checked the row's own honest disclosure that the end-seam at web:Ps.136.9|136.10 is content-only rather than grammatical: oshb:Ps.136.10 (“לְמַכֵּ֣ה מִ֭צְרַיִם…”) is itself still participial, so the true grammatical break in this recital's participial chain does not fall here at all — it falls later, at web:Ps.136.22|136.23, where a relative-clause finite verb takes over (see that seam at the row covering it). Because the medium confidence rating matches a content-driven rather than grammar-driven boundary, and the row discloses this honestly rather than overclaiming a grammatical marker that is not there, the span and its rationale hold up.

Re-swept the span from source: oshb:Ps.136.13's “לְגֹזֵ֣ר יַם ס֭וּף לִגְזָרִ֑ים…” collates at byte tier. Checked whether the participle/finite-verb alternation inside this span (participle at 136.10, finite verb at 136.11, participle again at 136.13, finite verbs at 136.14-15) undercuts the row's claim that grammatical form does not itself mark this row's edges; the same alternation recurs freely within a single row elsewhere in this recital too and is not treated as boundary-relevant there either, so the disclosure is consistent rather than selective. The end-seam (wilderness march named at web:Ps.136.16) is correctly read as a content pivot, matching the medium confidence rating.

The cross-psalm Sihon/Og claim was re-derived word by word from source bytes rather than trusted. The Sihon clause (oshb:Ps.135.11's opening words “לְסִיח֤וֹן מֶ֤לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֗י” against oshb:Ps.136.19's “לְ֭סִיחוֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֑י”) matches at the word level, differing only in cantillation, which is expected given each verse's differing clause position; the Og clause (oshb:Ps.135.11's “וּ֭לְעוֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן” against oshb:Ps.136.20's “וּ֭לְעוֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן”) is byte-identical, cantillation included. The land-grant clause was checked word by word in sequence (oshb:Ps.135.12 against oshb:Ps.136.21-22): of six words, exactly two differ — the third gains a lamed prefix (“לְנַחֲלָ֑ה” for the bare form in 135:12) and the sixth substitutes the word glossed 'his servant' for the word glossed 'his people' (“עַבְדּ֑וֹ” for the 135:12 form) — the row's "two words" count is exact. Considered whether an undisclosed participle-to-finite-verb shift inside this span (at 136.17|136.18) offers a rival seam; rejected on the same footing as the row's own reasoning — this alternation is not treated as boundary-relevant anywhere else in the recital, including in this writer's adjacent rows, so applying it only here would be an inconsistent standard.

Confirmed the voice shift at web:Ps.136.23 (first-person plural material against the third-person material running from 136.4 through 136.22) and the inclusio: the opening word of oshb:Ps.136.26 (“ה֭וֹדוּ”) and oshb:Ps.136.1 (“הוֹד֣וּ”) is the same lexeme, matching at every tier except full byte tier, where the two carry different disjunctive accents appropriate to each verse's own position — the row's own wording, "repeats … word for word," is a word-level claim and holds; it does not assert diacritic identity, so the accent difference is not a register defect. Short, tightly bounded closing unit; high confidence is warranted.

The four-verse communal-voice unit is real: checked oshb:Ps.137.1 (“עַ֥ל נַהֲר֨וֹת בָּבֶ֗ל שָׁ֣ם יָ֭שַׁבְנוּ גַּם…”) through 137.4 independently and confirmed no first-person-singular or direct second-person address appears before web:Ps.137.5's shift to "I." The quoted captors' demand at web:Ps.137.3 and the rhetorical refusal at web:Ps.137.4 are correctly kept inside the communal frame rather than treated as a separate voice, since the demand is reported within the narration rather than breaking it. The pmarks-based absence claim was checked directly against pmarks_Ps.json: neither this span nor the rest of Ps 137 carries any selah key at all, so the absence is correctly span-scoped and not a fabrication. One defect: the rejected_alternative's claim that the span has no addressee shift is an unquantified absence claim under the campaign's own universal-claim discipline, filed below.
